body:
# Independent audit: critical chord gauge and empty-corner contraction

Source:
`candidate 86934b651b11f7d5`.
Dependency read in full:
`candidate 6ac02348e3ceb9a9`.

**Result: PASS.** The author applied the sole wording repair in Section 1:
use the midpoint sum of the A section and the identified B subinterval.
The B subinterval is obtained by reflecting/translating the A section;
it is not reflected again. The displayed formulas were already correct.
No other repair identified.

## 1. Actual moment input and normalized chord coordinates

The supporting-facet condition is a necessary condition of genuine cap
criticality, not a freely assigned facet mean. Its fixed-mass moment body
for a one-dimensional facet is the interval of centers of actual
subintervals of the given length. Thus the prescribed mean is realized
by one whole subinterval here, even though higher-dimensional moment
bodies may require fractional selectors.

In the line coordinate x=y+t*Jv_i, Euclidean length equals ||v_i|| times
t-length. Therefore a_i,k_i,f_i are exactly the three t-lengths, and the
ratios in the moment equation are unchanged by normalization. Compatible
origins of the two endpoint cutting lines have midpoint y. The identified
B subinterval has center c_*=-c_A-(k_i/a_i)c_K and length a_i. Its
midpoint sum with the A section has center -k_i*c_K/(2a_i) and length
a_i. Actual midpoint compatibility puts that interval inside the actual
K chord. Interval containment gives k_i>=a_i and precisely

    |c_K|<=a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i).

The supporting B facet has positive length because a proper A section
has positive length and the genuine facet variation requires at least
that much available facet measure. No unrelated B center is substituted.

## 2. One genuine norm and the factor three

D=(K-y) intersect -(K-y) is a compact centrally symmetric convex body
with zero in its interior. Its gauge is a genuine norm: boundedness
ensures positive definiteness, the interior ensures finiteness, symmetry
gives N(-x)=N(x), and convexity gives the triangle inequality. The radial
parameter along Jv_i is exactly rho_i=k_i/2-|c_K|.

The chord inequality yields
rho_i>=(k_i^2+2a_i^2)/(2(k_i+2a_i))>=(k_i+2a_i)/6;
the second comparison is the identity 2(k_i-a_i)^2>=0. Also
rho_i<=k_i/2<=s_i/2. Hence 2lambda_i<=N(Jv_i)<=6lambda_i.
The linear relation Jv_1+Jv_2+Jv_3=0 takes place in this SAME norm,
so N(Jv_i)<=N(Jv_j)+N(Jv_k). Combining these inequalities gives
lambda_i<=3(lambda_j+lambda_k), equivalently lambda_i/Lambda<=3/4.
All nonunit-normal scaling factors match. No independent directional
norm or unproved balance assumption enters the argument.

## 3. Missing singletons and shell integration

The A thresholds have sum -sum h_B(v_i)<0, so their three halfspaces
cover the whole plane. If every unique-capture region is absent or null,
then almost every A point is captured at least twice. Its weighted load
is at least the smallest pair sum Lambda-lambda_max>=Lambda/4.
Every removed shell under a contraction about ANY p in A is a subset
of this same A; null exceptions stay null. Integrating the pointwise
load and differentiating the actual cap and total-volume formulas gives
sum lambda_i L_i(p)>=Lambda*a/2. Proper sections justify the C1 derivative,
and L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i.p)a_i has the correct coarea factor.

## 4. Exact scope of descent

The earlier independently audited fixed-facet implicit meeting-point
construction gives one actual menu covering the entire middle fiber
and common derivative -Lbar. With original global Q and strict endpoint
gaps, the two endpoint maxima stay below this upper certificate locally.
The derivative of its normalized budget is at most
-a/(2M)+2aQ/M^2, which is strictly less than -a/(18M) when Q/M<2/9.
Thus the actual optimized normalized depth decreases, even if displayed
caps cease to minimize after the contraction. The original deepest point
and all tested caps are actual mixed objects.

This gives a valid obstruction to an ATTAINED below-target local minimum
with the stated incidence pattern and endpoint gaps. The source does
not infer that every bad body has such a pattern, or that a tied endpoint
can be ignored. Those scope limitations are essential and retained.

## 5. Higher-dimensional incidence part

The final shell argument needs only a pointwise weighted capture-load
bound on A. Integrating on A minus A_t and differentiating yields exactly
d*a*tau and L_i=dU_i+(b_i-v_i.p)sigma_i. Proper section continuity gives
the derivative, with the interval case constant. For finitely many caps,
a nonempty capture set is either an allowed singleton or contains a
pair, so the stated minimum load is valid. This extends the incidence
argument, not the specifically planar gauge factor three. No unsupported
higher-dimensional chord-gauge analogue is claimed.

## 6. Added small deficient-corner reserve

The pointwise load inequality (8) is exact on singleton incidences and a
valid lower bound on every multiple incidence. If only one deficient
corner has positive area, choosing p in its actual closure preserves
every strict missed inequality under the contraction of that corner.
Thus the homothetic copy of the corner is contained in A_t intersect R,
giving the stated removed-corner upper bound. Weighted shell integration
then yields (10), and dropping its nonnegative 2lambda_j|R| term gives
Lbar>=(a-|R|)/2. The threshold |R|<=a/9 is therefore exactly sufficient
for 4a/9. All-null deficient corners allow arbitrary p. No separate
centers for different corners have been silently combined.

## 7. Exact corner derivative and simultaneous support optimum

For a positive-area corner, the pulled-back two thresholds have the
stated first derivatives b_j-v_j.p. A strip parallel to a proper cut
has pointwise stable membership in A except at the two endpoints of
its actual chord, and stable membership in the other halfspace except
at the unique crossing point. These are null tangential sets. Bounded
convergence on one common bounded coordinate interval therefore gives
the partial derivative equal to tau_ij, even if it is zero or the two
lines meet on the boundary of A. The intersection of the two changed
strips has O(t^2) area because the normals are independent. This proves
joint first-order expansion with both signs of threshold change.

Multiplication by (1-t)^2 gives
D_i(p)=2r_i-sum_(j!=i)(b_j-v_j.p)tau_ij exactly. It is nonnegative by
A_t subset A, and is at most 2r_i for p in the corner closure. Positive
corner area supplies an interior strict point; mixing it with any point
of the closed intersection proves the claimed equality of that
intersection with the closure. It is compact, so minimizing the affine
loss gives exactly (13), with the negative sign on the corner's support
function. The possible zero derivative for an unchanged local conical
corner is consistent with actual nested contraction.

Finally integrate the pointwise load inequality over the same removed
shell and insert these exact corner derivatives. The resulting lower
bound is affine in ONE p. Its support maximum over A is exactly (14),
including the sign of h_A(-sum c_i sum tau_ij v_j). Null corners are
legitimately omitted because their intersections with every shell have
zero area. The statement does not equate distinct corner minimizers or
assert an unproved sufficient numerical lower bound. Sections 6--7 PASS.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
